title: Unique compatible internal-Hom section lifts on affine opens
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent ideal, and $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ coherent modules [pqf-def-coherent]. Write $\mathcal P_n=\mathcal P/\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal P$ and $q_n^{\mathcal P}$ for the quotient projections and use the canonical transition maps [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Put $\mathcal H=\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Suppose $e_n:\mathcal H_n\to\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G_n,\mathcal F_n)$ satisfies $q_n^{\mathcal H}$ followed by $e_n$ and precomposition by $q_n^{\mathcal G}$ equals postcomposition by $q_n^{\mathcal F}$. Let $t_n:\mathcal G_n\to\mathcal F_n$ commute with every transition map. For any affine open $U\subseteq X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], there is exactly one family $s_n\in\mathcal H_n(U)$ commuting with all transition maps and satisfying $e_n(U)(s_n)=t_n|_U$ as a section of $\mathcal Hom(\mathcal G_n,\mathcal F_n)(U)$ for every $n\geq0$. Only sections over $U$ are asserted, not a global section or compatibility between distinct opens.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $J=\mathcal I(U)$, $N=\mathcal G(U)$, $M=\mathcal F(U)$, and $H=\operatorname{Hom}_A(N,M)$. The affine open is a spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with Noetherian section ring [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. The internal Hom is coherent [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-sheaf-hom-coherent]. Coherence gives quasi-coherence and finite type [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], so $N,M,H$ are finite by the affine sections comparison [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine]. The tilde-sections adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] identifies morphisms and sections over U with module linear maps. Ideal products and quotient sections identify with $J^{n+1}$-products and module quotients [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections]. The source quotient on affine sections is surjective, and precomposition by the quotient of G is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-completion-internal-hom-quotient]. Thus he forces $e_n(U)$ to be $h\bmod J^{n+1}H\mapsto (x\bmod J^{n+1}N\mapsto h(x)\bmod J^{n+1}M)$. The affine formal-module equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine] applies to these quotient systems.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine], compatible maps between the quotient systems on U identify with $\operatorname{Hom}_{A^\wedge}(N^\wedge,M^\wedge)$, and compatible source sections identify with $H^\wedge$. The evaluation map under these identifications is the componentwise map $\beta:(h_n)_n\mapsto ((x_n)_n\mapsto(h_n(x_n))_n)$. It is $A^\wedge$-linear since scalar multiplication and evaluation are componentwise. For $h\in H$, its value on the image of h in $H^\wedge$ is the completed linear map $h^\wedge$.

proof.text: For $P=N,M,H$, the canonical maps $c_P:A^\wedge\otimes_AP\to P^\wedge$ are natural linear bijections [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor]. The completed ring is flat [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat]; N is finite over the Noetherian A and thus finitely presented. Flat base change for Hom [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-hom-finitely-presented] gives the bijection $\theta:A^\wedge\otimes_AH\to\operatorname{Hom}_{A^\wedge}(A^\wedge\otimes_AN,A^\wedge\otimes_AM)$. Conjugation by $c_N,c_M$ gives a bijection $\gamma$ from its target to $\operatorname{Hom}_{A^\wedge}(N^\wedge,M^\wedge)$. Both $\beta c_H$ and $\gamma\theta$ are $A^\wedge$-linear and agree on $1\otimes h$: the former is $h^\wedge$ by the previous step and the latter is $h^\wedge$ by naturality of c. Such tensors generate, so $\beta=\gamma\theta c_H^{-1}$ is bijective. The restriction of t determines an element of its target by transition compatibility ht. Its unique preimage gives the asserted compatible section family on U. No global gluing is used.
